findings.where: First screen, the hero heading 'MARK · M · MOSELEY / INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR' (desktop-01, phone-01): a person's name in large red Roman capitals with interpuncts, on flat grey stone, under the big arch mark
findings.fault: A living person's name cut into grey stone in red Roman capitals reads as a monument, a memorial tablet or a heritage plaque. It does not read as an approachable advisor you could write to today. The page's first impression is grand and solemn rather than personal.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose brief asks for a personal, approachable advisor who is confident without big-firm claims (client values 1 and 6, brand sheet §5). Also a development-bank officer arriving from LinkedIn: a carved-inscription name makes the practice look ceremonial and remote, not like someone who takes on a mandate this month.

findings.where: First screen, the hero (desktop-01, phone-01): the logo mark fills the place where a person would stand, and the tile has no slot for a portrait anywhere
findings.fault: The direction shows the mark as the only picture and leaves no place for Mark's face. Nothing above the fold shows that a real, named person is behind the name, even as a labelled stand-in.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader choosing an individual consultant, who first wants to see the real person (first-visit-trust item 1). Mark, whose brief says 'the man himself — Mark is seen and heard' (client value 3), which every direction must answer.

findings.where: Article page specimen, the header (desktop-02, phone-02): 'MMM INFRA BLOG NO. 8 · 18 SEPTEMBER 2024' under the title, with no author line
findings.fault: The article is credited to the firm's blog and never names Mark. A reader who lands on the post from a shared link cannot tell that one experienced person wrote it, or who that person is.
findings.who_objects: A bank officer who follows a LinkedIn post straight to an article, and needs the author's name and a one-line bio before the piece counts as evidence of judgement (first-visit-trust item 12). Mark, whose brand is himself and not the firm (client value 1, §5).
